clips.title: Select nodes
clips.description: Hold Ctrl (Command on macOS) and click nodes to add them to the selection. Click a selected node with the same modifier to remove it.
transcript: Hold Ctrl / ⌘ and click two nodes to select them
Keep holding Ctrl / ⌘ and click another node to add it
Ctrl / ⌘ + click a selected node again to remove it

clips.title: Move a selection
clips.description: Select two nodes with Ctrl/Command-click, release the modifier, then drag either selected node. Both move together and retain their new positions.
transcript: Ctrl / ⌘ + click to select nodes
Release Ctrl / ⌘, then drag either selected node
Both nodes keep their new positions; other nodes stay put

clips.title: Release a moved node
clips.description: Move a node, select it through Moved, and release its manual fixation while retaining its current position.
transcript: Drag a node to fix it in a new position
Click Moved to select the fixed node
Click Release to remove its fixed position
The node stays here; Moved returns to 0

clips.title: Reset moved nodes
clips.description: Drag a node, click Moved to select manually positioned nodes, then click Reset to restore their original positions. Undo can reverse the reset.
transcript: Drag a node to a new position
Click Moved to select the node you dragged
Click Reset to restore its original position
Click Undo to return to the dragged position

clips.title: Select with a rectangle
clips.description: Hold Ctrl or Command and drag the canvas background around nodes to replace the selection.
transcript: Ctrl / ⌘ + click a node to start a selection
Ctrl / ⌘ + drag the background around two other nodes
The rectangle replaces the selection with these two nodes

clips.title: Rotate a selection
clips.description: Select at least two elements, then hold Ctrl or Command and scroll to rotate them around the pointer.
transcript: Ctrl / ⌘ + click to select nodes
Hold Ctrl / ⌘ and scroll to rotate around the pointer
Both nodes keep their rotated positions

clips.title: Place a text annotation
clips.description: Create a text label, then drag its unpositioned list entry onto the drawing.
transcript: Open the text annotation dialog
Enter Binding site as the annotation text
Turn on Bold to emphasize the label
Click OK to add the label to the list
The ? means unpositioned. Drag the label onto the drawing
The target icon confirms the label is positioned

clips.title: Import FASTA input
clips.description: Paste two FASTA records, inspect the parsed sequences, structures, and names, then render them.
transcript: Open FASTA Data to import RNA records
Paste two FASTA records with sequences and structures
Check the parsed sequences, structures, and names
Click OK to render the imported RNA

clips.title: Apply a probability profile
clips.description: Enter profile values, choose biological start-index coordinates, and apply the nucleotide color gradient.
transcript: Enter each nucleotide index and its probability for RNA 1.
Choose Start 1: indices are -2, -1, 1, 2, skipping zero.
Uncheck =1 so purple represents zero; higher values fade the overlay.
Click Apply to color RNA 1 using the probability profile.
Lower probabilities have stronger purple shading on RNA 1.

clips.title: Store and load a session
clips.description: Download the current JSON session, clear the viewer, and load the file to restore the figure.
transcript: Click Store to download this session as a JSON file
Click Clear to empty the inputs and remove the figure
Click Load, then choose vaRRI_session.json in the file picker
The saved inputs and RNA figure are restored

clips.title: Export a publication PNG
clips.description: Set pixel dimensions and print density in the PNG export dialog, then download the image.
transcript: Click PNG to choose image size and print density
Set width to 1200 pixels; height follows the aspect ratio
Set DPI to 300; the pixel dimensions stay the same
Click Export PNG to download the image
PNG downloaded: 1200 × 901 pixels at 300 DPI

clips.title: Add a paired region highlight
clips.description: Enter one range for each RNA strand and add a translucent paired-region highlight.
transcript: Click Add in Region Highlights
Enter 1-2 for the first RNA strand
Enter 3-4 for its partner on the second RNA
Set opacity to 0.5 for a translucent highlight
Click OK to add the highlight to the drawing
The paired region is highlighted and listed on the left

clips.title: Choose an example
clips.description: Choose Mutations & highlighting to load its RNA input, four mutations, and a subsequence highlight.
transcript: Open Example to browse the built-in examples
Choose Mutations & highlighting
The inputs and figure include four mutations and a green highlight

clips.title: Name and number a strand
clips.description: Commit a strand name and a negative biological start index, with numbering that skips zero.
transcript: Name the first strand Leader RNA, then press Enter
Set Start 1 to -2, then press Enter
Numbering skips zero between -1 and 1

clips.title: Add a subsequence highlight
clips.description: Choose the second strand and highlight biological positions 102–103 at half opacity.
transcript: Click Add in Subsequence Highlights
Choose Seq. 2 for the second RNA strand
Enter biological range 102-103
Set opacity to 0.5
Click OK to add the highlight
The purple range is highlighted and listed

clips.title: Annotate a point mutation
clips.description: Annotate G102A on the second strand of the supplied structure without editing the input sequence or predicting a fold.
transcript: Click Add in Point Mutations to annotate the supplied structure
Choose Seq. 2 for the second RNA strand
Enter biological position 102
Enter A in To for the replacement annotation
Click OK to add the G102A annotation
G102A adds a green outline and A label; inputs stay unchanged and no fold is predicted

clips.title: Highlight RRI nucleotides
clips.description: Compare outlines around all ten interaction-region nucleotides with the eight paired nucleotides, excluding the two unpaired A bases.
transcript: Choose region for RRI nucleotide highlighting
Region outlines all 10 nucleotides, including both unpaired A bases
Choose basepairs to outline only paired nucleotides
Basepairs outlines 8 nucleotides; both unpaired A bases lose the red outline

clips.title: Highlight the RRI background
clips.description: Use the RRI background dropdown to generate one whole-region highlight, separate paired-stack highlights, or remove the automatic highlights.
transcript: Choose region: this dropdown controls automatic RRI backgrounds
Region adds one generated highlight: 1-5&1-5
Choose basepairs to separate the two paired stacks
Two generated highlights leave the unpaired A bases clear
Choose nothing to remove the automatic highlights
The generated entries and backgrounds are gone; the input is unchanged

clips.title: Make the RRI horizontal
clips.description: Enable Linear horizontal RRI layout to create stable paired rails while Force layout stays off.
transcript: With Force layout off, enable Linear horizontal RRI layout
Paired bases now form horizontal rails; Force layout stays off
